title: Map export
description: B5: a world's map export, which the plugin writes into the directory its config names (B12) and world render reads. The directory holds two files: raster.bin, the map, and meta.json, this document, which says which world the raster shows and how to read it. The plugin writes each to a temporary file in the directory, then renames it into place: raster.bin first and meta.json last, so a meta.json always follows the raster it describes. The directory may hold other files, among them the dot-prefixed temporary files of a write in progress: a reader ignores every file but meta.json and the raster it names, and reacts only to meta.json. A reader rejects a meta.json whose raster.bytes is not size * size * 10. It trusts a raster only when the file's length and SHA-256 match meta.json's raster; a mismatch means the raster was taken while the export was being rewritten, or that a rewrite was interrupted, and the reader treats the export as bad and keeps its last good render. RASTER LAYOUT: the frame is world space, so a position maps to a pixel with no projection. The raster is square, size by size pixels, covering x from -half_width up to but not including +half_width metres, and z from +half_width down to but not including -half_width, each a half-open range that includes the edge its row or column 0 starts at; a position outside it falls off the raster. Row 0 is north, the largest z, and column 0 is west, the smallest x. Pixel (column, row) samples the world at its centre: x = -half_width + (column + 0.5) * pitch and z = half_width - (row + 0.5) * pitch, where pitch = 2 * half_width / size. A position (x, z) falls in column floor((x + half_width) / pitch) and row floor((half_width - z) / pitch). The file is planar, little-endian and row-major, with three planes one after the other, each size * size values in row order: biome as uint16, then height as float32 in metres, then forest factor as float32. Its length is size * size * 10 bytes. Biome holds the game's biome flag value: see $defs/biome. Height is the world generator's terrain height, and height and forest factor are always finite; a pixel at or below water_level is water. Forest factor is the world generator's own, in which a lower value is denser forest, and forest is where it is below 1.15.

seed.description: What identifies the world's terrain: the game keeps the seed as a string and as the integer the world generator uses, and the plugin writes both.

name.description: The seed string, which may be empty.

value.description: The seed the world generator uses.

generator_version.description: The world generator's version, the game's world generation version number: the same seed gives a different map under another version.

water_level.description: The water level in metres, as the game states it: a height at or below it is water.

size.description: The raster's width and height in pixels.

half_width.description: Half the raster's width in metres: it covers x and z from -half_width to +half_width, centred on the origin.

raster.description: The raster file this document describes.

file.description: The raster's file name, in the same directory.

bytes.description: The raster's length in bytes: size * size * 10.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the raster's bytes, in lower-case hex.

biome.description: The values of the raster's biome plane: the game's biome flags, by the game's names. A raster holds no other value.
